metadata.description: Two-week progress review (weeks of Aug 17 and Aug 24, 2026) for MEDAS 2.0 (pre-release). Akshit's role: automate deployment for the backend, which is built and deployed to Cloud Run by hand today; his dev setup deploys automatically on a git tag. Unblocked Darshil's frontend CI/CD with a new repo and GCP dev access, planned dev and stage with Jiang, then prioritized fixing the crash-looping dev backend (stale MongoDB URI) with a separate dev MongoDB created with Prof. Tayyar Haitham, verified Aug 27, and documented it in MEDAS-docs. Next: stage.
metadata.note: Evidence: B04 and B07 are Akshit's own screenshots, cropped; request URLs in B07 removed. No chat messages shown. Dev database holds example test data only.

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW -- hesitant writer; single-word trigger (the component matches single words only)
beats.narration_text: Two busy weeks, mostly spent unblocking: giving a teammate what he needed to build the frontend pipeline, and fixing a broken dev backend so testing could finally start.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer typing bookend (EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW): the overview accumulates token by token, so mid-beat frames are mostly cream by design.

beats.narration_text: Some context. MEDAS is a diagnostic advising system for emergency physicians, and I work on its deployment. Right now, Jiang builds the backend logic, then creates Docker images and deploys them to Cloud Run by hand. My dev setup does that automatically: push a git tag, and the image is built and deployed for you.

props.footerNote: Today these steps are done by hand. The dev setup runs them on every git tag.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK beat -- the weekly rhythm, shown before the work
beats.narration_text: Here's the rhythm behind the work. Every Monday, two hours with the whole team, across all the MEDAS systems. Every Thursday, two hours with just the Aggregation System team. Between meetings, I build, fix, and write it down in a MEDAS docs repo I created, so every incident and setup step has a record. Two weeks, four meetings, eight hours of syncs.

artifactLines: Monday: two hours with the whole team, which brings together all of the MEDAS systems.
Thursday: two hours with the Aggregation System team.
Between meetings: build, fix, and write it down.
Record: MEDAS-docs, a repo I created for incidents and setup instructions, so every fix has a written record that anyone on the team can check later.
Two weeks: four meetings and eight hours of syncs, across the weeks of August 17 and August 24.

beats.role_note: Akshit's own screenshot: dev-branch commit history (cropped)
beats.narration_text: Week one. Darshil was ready to build the frontend's CI/CD pipeline, but there was no repo to build it in. On August nineteenth I created medas aggregation frontend and pushed the initial code. The next day, his Dockerfile and Cloud Run deploy workflow landed, and by August thirtieth, his CI and rollback workflows were merged.

A repo alone wasn't enough. Darshil also needed access, so I gave him permissions on the GCP dev project and added him as a collaborator. That meant he could deploy to the dev environment himself, instead of waiting on me for every step.

props.footerNote: Darshil built the frontend CI/CD. My part was clearing the way.

beats.role_note: dev vs stage plan with Jiang
beats.narration_text: In the same week, Jiang and I planned the environments: dev first, then stage. My backend dev automation was in place, and we agreed I'll take the backend stage setup next, while Darshil works on the frontend side.

beats.role_note: Akshit's own screenshot: real Cloud Run logs 2026-08-27 (cropped, request URLs removed)
beats.narration_text: Week two brought a blocker. Jiang couldn't test the dev setup at all, because the dev backend returned Service Unavailable on every request. The Cloud Run logs show why: gunicorn starts, a worker boots, crashes seconds later, and the service shuts down. Then it starts again, and fails the same way.

The dev database secret pointed at an old MongoDB cluster that no longer existed. So I made this the priority. I worked with Professor Tayyar Haitham to create a separate dev MongoDB, seeded it with example test data, and updated the secret. By August twenty-seventh, logins were succeeding again, and dev testing was unblocked.

props.eyebrow: WEEK OF AUG 24 · THE PRIORITY FIX
props.footerNote: No real patient data: the dev database holds example test data only.

beats.narration_text: Then I wrote it down. Incident one, the stale MongoDB URI, is in the MEDAS docs repo: the symptom, the diagnosis, the root cause, and the fix. The next person who sees Service Unavailable on dev will know to open the Cloud Run logs first.

artifactLines: Symptom: Service Unavailable on every request to the dev backend, even /health.
Diagnosis: secrets checked first, then the Cloud Run logs, then the traceback.
Root cause: a stale MONGODB_URI secret pointing at a cluster that no longer existed.
Fix: a new dev MongoDB cluster under the institutional Atlas account and a new version of the secret, verified August 27.
Lesson: when dev says Service Unavailable, open the Cloud Run logs first, before the application code.

beats.role_note: the two-week scorecard with an honest caveat; narration discusses, does not recite
beats.narration_text: Put together, the two weeks come down to one thing: removing blockers. Darshil could build his pipeline because the repo and access were ready. Jiang can test on dev because the database is fixed. And the honest caveat: the automation is proven on dev only. Stage isn't built yet, and that's my next step.
